notes: Model routing for Claude runtimes lives in 'tiers'; routing for Codex runtimes / codex-exec cross-dispatch lives in 'codex_tiers' (see references/model-routing-codex.md); Gemini in 'gemini_tiers' (references/model-routing-gemini.md); Grok in 'grok_tiers' (references/model-routing-grok.md). Other runtimes map the abstract tiers onto their own lineup — see 'Portability & Model Routing' in SKILL.md.

Tier order: cheap < standard < strong < heavy < deep. 'heavy' (added 2026-09-22) = one rung below deep: gpt-6.1-sol max on Codex (gpt-6-astra high until 2026-09-30), Opus 5.5 at xhigh on Claude (keeps the Fable budget for risk surface; Opus tops out at xhigh, so on Claude heavy runs the same model and effort as strong). Runtimes with no rung between strong and deep (Grok, Gemini) map heavy UP to their deep settings.

Claude floor is Sonnet 5.5 (Bogdan 2026-09-29: 'with sonnet 5.5 being good, we can use it as the lowest allowed claude model'). Sonnet 5.5 runs 'search' and 'cheap' (triage, trivial pass, patch application); every review dimension runs on Opus 5.5 (standard/strong/heavy) or Fable 5.1 (deep). Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 are not used for any review role. Haiku 5.5 takes simple tasks once it ships. Sonnet and Opus top out at xhigh, never max (Bogdan 2026-09-29: 'they perform their best at xhigh'); max is Fable-only on Claude.
limits.max_concurrent_agents caps SIMULTANEOUS dispatches, not the total. A large PR may select 12 agents; launch them in waves of <= max_concurrent_agents and queue the rest.
fallback: null means: on refusal/failure, record the dimension as 'no coverage — degraded' in the report and continue. Never abort the run.

Per-runtime task overrides: a task may carry a 'codex' block ({tier, effort}) that replaces the task's tier/effort ONLY for Codex runtimes / codex-exec cross-dispatch. Resolution order on Codex: task.codex.effort > task.codex.tier's codex effort > task.effort > codex_tiers[tier].effort. Other runtimes ignore the block.

Effort policy (Bogdan 2026-09-22): Opus 5.5 and gpt-6-sol are cheaper than what they replaced, so spend the savings on effort; never lower effort to exploit newer-model efficiency. Task efforts were each raised one rung that day. If a runtime lacks a requested level, round UP to the nearest one it supports (e.g. Gemini xhigh -> max) except where a ceiling applies (grok-4.7 tops at xhigh). Ceiling (Bogdan 2026-09-29): Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 top out at xhigh, never max; Fable 5.1 keeps max on deep. Codex (Bogdan 2026-09-30): gpt-6-astra tops out at xhigh for now; gpt-6.1-sol may run max (heavy tier, deep fallback).

search.notes: Claude-only helper role, not a review tier: codebase search / file location / exploration subagents (e.g. Explore). Never produces findings. Sonnet 5.5 replaced Sonnet 5 on 2026-09-29.

cheap.notes: Triage, patch application, trivial pass. Sonnet 5.5 (the Claude floor, $2/$10) replaced Opus 5.5 medium on 2026-09-29; half the price, so the savings go into effort (medium -> high). Sonnet 5.5 carries five refusal categories (cyber, bio, frontier_llm, reasoning_extraction, general_harms), so cheap tasks fall back to 'standard' (Opus 5.5).

standard.notes: Core review workhorse for all standard dimensions (logic, silent failure, tests, performance, types, style, comments). Opus 5.5 is Fable-5.1-class on most benchmarks at $4/$20 (cheaper than Opus 5). Its API default effort is 'medium' (Opus 5 was 'high'), so always state the effort explicitly.

strong.notes: Coordinator, adjudication, universal fallback, and deep-tier overflow once max_fable_dispatches is spent (effort high/xhigh). Opus 5.5 carries broader safety classifiers than Opus 5 (cyber + bio + reasoning_extraction), so keep coordinator prose neutral and let the refusal loop handle leaves.

heavy.notes: One rung below deep: large-PR deep dives, deep-tier fallback, Fable-cap overflow. Opus 5.5 at xhigh, its ceiling (Bogdan 2026-09-29: no Opus max), so on Claude this matches strong; it spends no max_fable_dispatches slot. Effort is prompt-encoded on Claude Code.

deep.notes: Risk-surface review (security, migrations) and architectural deep dives. Refusal fallback is Opus 5.5 (strong). Mandatory 30-day retention, no ZDR. Most expensive tier ($10/$50), so it stays capped by max_fable_dispatches.

codex_tiers.notes: Always pass -m and model_reasoning_effort explicitly (never inherit ~/.codex/config.toml defaults). Review leaves run '-s read-only'. Lineup (Bogdan 2026-09-30: 'use sol 6.1 for as much as possible, cheap and capable, astra 6 at the very top for now (xhigh)'): gpt-6.1-sol runs cheap, standard, strong and heavy, split by effort (high / high / xhigh / max); gpt-6-astra runs only deep, at xhigh. gpt-6.1-sol (released 2026-09-29, $2/$10 per 1M in/out, cached input $0.10) nearly matches gpt-6-astra ($10/$50) on agentic coding at a fifth of the price. It needs Codex CLI >= 0.159 (0.158 rejects the ID on a ChatGPT login); live-probed 2026-09-30, efforts low..max plus 'ultra'. Fallback chain when a gpt-6.1-sol dispatch errors: gpt-6-sol at the same effort, then gpt-5.6-terra. gpt-6-luna is off the review routing. Fallbacks stay within GPT-6.1, GPT-6 and 5.6; never route to gpt-5.5 or older. Verify IDs against ~/.codex/models_cache.json after any model-generation bump.

cheap.notes: Triage, mechanical checks, patch application, plus style/comment review via task overrides. gpt-6.1-sol replaced gpt-6-luna on 2026-09-30 (sol 6.1 for everything below the top). Same model and default effort as standard: on Codex the two tiers now differ only through per-task efforts.

standard.notes: Most review dimensions; effort 'high' up to 'xhigh' (logic and silent-failure run xhigh). Replaced gpt-6-sol on 2026-09-30 at the same $2/$10 price. Fallback: gpt-6-sol at the same effort, then gpt-5.6-terra.

strong.notes: Adjudication-grade review and universal fallback; effort 'xhigh' up to 'max' (same model as standard, one effort band up). Also the vision tier (attach images with -i). Fallback: gpt-6-sol at the same effort.

heavy.notes: One rung below deep: large-PR deep dives, fallback when a deep (astra xhigh) dispatch fails, heavier adjudication. Was gpt-6-astra high until 2026-09-30; astra is now reserved for deep, and gpt-6.1-sol at max costs a fifth of astra. Fallback: gpt-6-sol max.

deep.notes: Risk-surface review (security, migrations): the only tier on astra. xhigh is the ceiling for now (Bogdan 2026-09-30); run 'max' or 'ultra' (subagent fan-out) only when explicitly requested. Fallback: gpt-6.1-sol (effort: max).

gemini_tiers.notes: Model routing for Gemini runtimes (Gemini CLI, Antigravity). Maps abstract tiers to Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro (3.8 Pro is not yet available).

cheap.notes: Triage, mechanical checks, patch application with low reasoning.

standard.notes: Most review dimensions (logic, silent failure, style, comment, tests) with high reasoning.

strong.notes: Coordinator, adjudication, universal fallback (highest-tier Pro model available).

heavy.notes: No rung between strong (high) and deep (max) on Gemini: heavy maps up to deep settings.

deep.notes: Risk-surface review (security, migrations) with maximum reasoning depth.

grok_tiers.notes: Model routing for xAI / Grok runtimes. All tiers on grok-4.7 (released 2026-09-21; 500K context, $2/$6), differentiated by effort. grok-4.7 accepts ONLY low|medium|high|xhigh -- 'max' is rejected by the CLI (live-probed 2026-09-22). Fallback grok-4.6 at the same effort; never 4.5. grok-4.7-build-fast is 2x the price -- latency only, not a cheap tier.

cheap.notes: Triage, mechanical checks, patch application with minimal reasoning.

heavy.notes: xhigh is grok-4.7's ceiling, so heavy maps up to deep settings.

deep.notes: Risk-surface review (security, migrations) at the highest effort grok-4.7 accepts.
